questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 519 km in 7 hours. If he covers two-third of his distance in 5/7 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining distance = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 of total distance

Remaining time = 1 − 5/7 = 2/7 of total time

Remaining distance = 519 × 1/3 = 173 km

Remaining time = 7 × 2/7 = 2 hours

Required speed = 173 ÷ 2 = 86.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 86.5 km/hr.**

Average Speed

It is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

questions.question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 74 km/hr at an interval of 28 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 10 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of cabs (V꜀) = 74 km/hr

Time interval between cabs starting (T꜀) = 28 minutes

Time interval at which the man meets the cabs (Tₘ) = 10 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative speed when moving in opposite directions = Sum of individual speeds

**Calculation:**

T꜀ = 28 minutes = (28)/(60) hours = (7)/(15) hours

Tₘ = 10 minutes = (10)/(60) hours = (1)/(6) hours

The distance between two consecutive cabs is the distance covered by the first cab in the interval before the second cab starts.

Distance between cabs = V꜀ × T꜀

Distance between cabs = 74 × (28)/(60) km

Let the speed of the man be Vₘ km/hr.

Since the man is moving in the opposite direction to the cabs, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (V꜀ + Vₘ).

The man meets the two cabs at an interval of Tₘ (10 minutes). This means the distance between the cabs is covered by their relative speed in 10 minutes.

Distance between cabs = (V꜀ + Vₘ) × Tₘ

Distance between cabs = (74 + V_m) × (10)/(60) km

**Equate the expressions for the distance between cabs and solve for Vₘ.**

74 × (28)/(60) = (74 + V_m) × (10)/(60)

74 × 28 = (74 + Vₘ) × 10

2072 = 740 + 10Vₘ

2072 - 740 = 10Vₘ

1332 = 10Vₘ

V_m = (1332)/(10)

Vₘ = 133.2 km/hr

**∴ The speed of the man is 133.2 km/hr.**

questions.question: A boat takes 51 minutes to go 10.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 7 : 6. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 17.7 km upstream and 66.3 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Upstream time = 51 minutes = 51 ÷ 60 = 0.85 hours

Upstream distance = 10.2 km

Speed ratio (boat : stream) = 7 : 6

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Upstream speed = Boat speed − Stream speed

Downstream speed = Boat speed + Stream speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed = 10.2 ÷ 0.85 = 12 km/hr

Let boat speed = 7x, stream speed = 6x ⇒ upstream = 7x − 6x = x

⇒ x = 12 ⇒ boat speed = 7x = 84 km/hr, stream speed = 6x = 72 km/hr

⇒ Downstream speed = 84 + 72 = 156 km/hr

⇒ Time for 17.7 km upstream = 17.7 ÷ 12 = 1.475 hours

⇒ Time for 66.3 km downstream = 66.3 ÷ 156 = 0.425 hours

⇒ Total time = 1.475 + 0.425 = 1.9 hours

**∴ Total time taken = 1.9 hours**

questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 387 km in 21 hours. If he covers two - thirds of this distance in 5/7 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance in the time left ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 387 km

Total time = 21 hours

**Formula used:**

Remaining distance = Total − Covered

Remaining time = Total time − Time used

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

Distance covered = 2/3 of 387 = 258 km

Time used = 5/7 of 21 = 15 hours

⇒ Remaining distance = 387 − 258 = 129 km

⇒ Remaining time = 21 − 15 = 6 hours

⇒ Required speed = 129 ÷ 6 = 21.5 km/h

**∴ Required speed = 21.5 km/h**

questions.question: Mr. W travelled 370 km, 390 km and 720 km at speeds of 37 km/hr, 5 km/hr and 8 km/hr, respectively. Find his average speed in km/hr.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance 1 (d₁) = 370 km

Speed 1 (s₁) = 37 km/hr

Distance 2 (d₂) = 390 km

Speed 2 (s₂) = 5 km/hr

Distance 3 (d₃) = 720 km

Speed 3 (s₃) = 8 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Total Distance = d₁ + d₂ + d₃

Total Time = (d₁ / s₁) + (d₂ / s₂) + (d₃ / s₃)

**Calculations:**

Total Distance = 370 + 390 + 720

⇒ Total Distance = 1480 km

Total Time = (370 / 37) + (390 / 5) + (720 / 8)

⇒ Total Time = 10 + 78 + 90

⇒ Total Time = 178 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 1480 / 178 = 740 / 89

⇒ Average Speed = 8(28)/(89) km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 753 km in 12 hours. If he covers two-thirds of the distance in 2/3 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time left ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 753 km

Total time = 12 hours

Distance covered in the first part = (2)/(3) of total distance

Time taken for the first part = (2)/(3) of total time

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = (Distance)/(Time)

**Calculations:**

Distance covered in the first part = (2)/(3) times 753

⇒ Distance covered = 502 km

Remaining distance = Total distance - Distance covered in the first part

⇒ Remaining distance = 753 - 502

⇒ Remaining distance = 251 km

Time taken for the first part = (2)/(3) times 12

⇒ Time taken = 2 × 4

⇒ Time taken = 8 hours

Remaining time = Total time - Time taken for the first part

⇒ Remaining time = 12 - 8

⇒ Remaining time = 4 hours

Speed required to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time = (Remaining distance)/(Remaining time)

⇒ Speed = (251)/(4)

⇒ Speed = 62.75 km/hr

**∴ The speed should be 62.75 km/hr to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time.**

questions.question: In a 2295 m circular race, Siddharth finishes one round in 85 seconds and Yash finishes one round in 45 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Track length = 2295 m

Siddharth's time per round = 85 seconds

Yash's time per round = 45 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Number of distinct meeting points (opposite directions) = Sum of ratio terms of speeds (in lowest terms)

**Calculations:**

Siddharth's speed = 2295 / 85 = 27 m/s

Yash's speed = 2295 / 45 = 51 m/s

Ratio of speeds = 27 : 51 = 9 : 17

Number of meeting points = 9 + 17

⇒ Number of meeting points = 26

**∴ The number of different meeting points on the circumference is 26.**

questions.question: Babita travels a certain distance at a speed of 11 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 44 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 34 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Babita travels distance x at 11 km/h

Then 2x at 44 km/h

Average speed for full journey (6x) = 34 km/h

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Time for x at 11 km/h = x ÷ 11

Time for 2x at 44 km/h = 2x ÷ 44 = x ÷ 22

Total time for going = x ÷ 11 + x ÷ 22 = 3x ÷ 22

Total distance of full journey = 3x + 3x = 6x

Total time = 6x ÷ 34 = 3x ÷ 17

Time for return = Total time − time for going ⇒ 3x ÷ 17 − 3x ÷ 22

LCM of 17 and 22 = 374

⇒ Time for return = (66x − 51x) ÷ 374 = 15x ÷ 374

Return distance = 3x

Return speed = 3x ÷ (15x ÷ 374) = 3x × 374 ÷ 15x ⇒ 1122 ÷ 15 = 74.8 km/h

**∴ The speed of return journey is 74.8 km/hr.**

Distance covered = (7)/(9) of the remaining distance

Then remaining distance = 54 - x

x = (7/9) × (54 - x)

questions.question: Walking at (2)/(7) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 70 minutes late in reaching.The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the usual time taken by Abhijeet to cover the distance be t minutes.

Abhijeet walks at 2/7 of his normal speed and is 70 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time be t.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 2/7 of his normal speed, the speed becomes (2/7) × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (2/7 × S) = (7 × t) ÷ 2

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (7 × t) ÷ 2 - t

Given, the difference in time is 70 minutes:

(7t ÷ 2) - t = 70

⇒ (7t ÷ 2) - (2t ÷ 2) = 70

⇒ 5t ÷ 2 = 70

⇒ t = 70 × 2 / 5 = 28

**∴ The usual time taken by Abhijeet is 28 minutes.**

questions.question: Walking at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 28 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his destination is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Abhijeet walks at 2/3 of his normal speed and is 28 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let normal time be t minutes.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 2/3 of his normal speed, the new speed becomes 2/3 × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (2/3 × S) = (3 × t) ÷ 2

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (3 × t) ÷ 2 - t

Given, the difference in time is 28 minutes:

(3t ÷ 2) - t = 28

⇒ t ÷ 2 = 28

⇒ t = 56

**∴ The usual time taken by Abhijeet is 56 minutes.**

questions.question: Walking at (2)/(5) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 48 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his destination is?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Walking speed = (2/5) of normal speed

Time difference = 48 minutes

**Formula used:**

Let the usual time taken = T (in minutes).

New time taken = (5/2) × T

Time difference = New time - Usual time

**Calculation:**

48 = (5/2) × T - T

⇒ 48 = (5T - 2T)/2

⇒ 48 = 3T/2

⇒ T = (48 × 2)/3 = 32 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: "Walking at (2)/(5) of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 18 minutes late in reach. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and destination is:

questions.question: The downstream speed is 41 km/hr and the upstream speed is 20.5 km/hr. It takes a boat a total of 13 hours to go to a place and come back. What is the total distance travelled by the boat?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Downstream speed = 41 km/hr

Upstream speed = 20.5 km/hr

Total time taken = 13 hours

Calculation:

Let the distance travelled in one direction be D km.

Time taken for downstream journey = dfrac{D}{41} hours

Time taken for upstream journey = dfrac{D}{20.5} hours

Total time = downstream time + upstream time = 13 hours

dfrac{D}{41} + dfrac{D}{20.5} = 13

dfrac{D}{41} + dfrac{2D}{41} = 13

dfrac{3D}{41} = 13

⇒ 3D = 13 × 41

⇒ 3D = 533

⇒ D = dfrac{533}{3}

The total distance travelled by the boat is the distance to the place and back,

So total distance = 2 × D = 2 × (533)/(3) = (1066)/(3) {km}

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Train A, running at a speed of 32 km/hr, takes 33 seconds to completely cross train B, running at 28 km/hr in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B crosses a bridge completely in 54 seconds. What is the length of the bridge (in m)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Train A = 32 km/hr = (32 times 1000)/(3600) m/s = 80/9 m/s

Speed of Train B = 28 km/hr = (28 times 1000)/(3600) m/s = 70/9 m/s

Time taken to cross each other = 33 seconds

Length of Train B = 1.5 × Length of Train A

Train B crosses a bridge in 54 seconds

**Formula used:**

For two trains crossing in opposite directions: Combined speed = Speed of Train A + Speed of Train B

Total distance covered = Length of Train A + Length of Train B

For Train B crossing a bridge: Total distance = Length of Train B + Length of Bridge

**Calculation:**

Let the length of Train A = L meters. Then, length of Train B = 1.5L meters.

Combined speed = 80/9 + 70/9 = 150/9 m/s = 50/3 m/s

⇒ Total distance = Length of Train A + Length of Train B = L + 1.5L = 2.5L

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ 33 = (2.5L)/(frac{50){3}}

⇒ 7.5L = 33 × 50

⇒ L = (1650)/(7.5)

⇒ L = 220 meters

Length of Train A = 220 m

Length of Train B = 1.5 × 220 = 330 m

For Train B crossing a bridge:

⇒ Total distance = Length of Train B + Length of Bridge

⇒ 54 = frac{330 + {Length of Bridge}}{(70)/(9)}

⇒ 330 + Length of Bridge = 54 × (70/9)

⇒ 330 + Length of Bridge = 420

⇒ Length of Bridge = 420 - 330

⇒ Length of Bridge = 90 meters

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The downstream speed is 22 km/hr and the upstream speed is 5.5 km/hr. It takes a boat a total of 8 hours to go to a place and come back. What is the total distance travelled by the boat?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Downstream speed = 22 km/hr

Upstream speed = 5.5 km/hr

Total time = 8 hours

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

Total distance = Distance downstream + Distance upstream

**Calculation:**

Let the one-way distance be D km.

Time taken downstream = D / 22

Time taken upstream = D / 5.5

Total time = Time downstream + Time upstream

⇒ 8 = D / 22 + D / 5.5

⇒ 8 = (D / 22) + (4D / 22)

⇒ 8 = (5D / 22)

⇒ D = (8 × 22) / 5

⇒ D = 176 / 5

Total distance = 2 × D

⇒ Total distance = 2 × (176 / 5)

⇒ Total distance = 352 / 5 km

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A boat takes 83 minutes to go 33.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 8 : 5. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 47.1 km upstream and 55.9 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time to cover 33.2 km upstream = 83 minutes = 83 ÷ 60 = 1.383 hours

Ratio of boat speed to stream speed = 8 : 5

Find total time for: 47.1 km upstream + 55.9 km downstream

**Formula used:**

Upstream speed = B − S

Downstream speed = B + S

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

Let boat speed = 8x, stream speed = 5x

⇒ Upstream speed = 8x − 5x = 3x

⇒ 33.2 ÷ 3x = 1.383

⇒ 3x = 33.2 ÷ 1.383 = 24

⇒ x = 8

⇒ Boat speed = 8x = 64 km/h

⇒ Stream speed = 5x = 40 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = 64 − 40 = 24 km/h

⇒ Downstream speed = 64 + 40 = 104 km/h

Time for 47.1 km upstream = 47.1 ÷ 24 = 1.9625 hours

Time for 55.9 km downstream = 55.9 ÷ 104 = 0.5375 hours

Total time = 1.9625 + 0.5375 = 2.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5 hours**

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(7) of his normal speed, Manish is 20 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance be t minutes.

Manish walks at 5/7 of his normal speed and is 20 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time be t.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 5/7 of his normal speed, the speed becomes (5/7) × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (5/7 × S) = (7 × t) ÷ 5

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (7 × t) ÷ 5 - t

Given, the difference in time is 20 minutes:

(7t ÷ 5) - t = 20

⇒ (7t ÷ 5) - (5t ÷ 5) = 20

⇒ 2t ÷ 5 = 20

⇒ t = 20 × 5 / 2 = 50 minutes

**∴ The usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance is 50 minutes.**

questions.question: In a 2100 m circular race, Amit finishes one round in 42 seconds and Sumit finishes one round in 75 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

Track length = 2100 m

Amit's time per round = 42 seconds

Sumit's time per round = 75 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Number of distinct meeting points (opposite directions) = (Speed of Person 1 + Speed of Person 2) / GCD(Speed of Person 1, Speed of Person 2)

**Calculations:**

Amit's speed = 2100 m / 42 s = 50 m/s

Sumit's speed = 2100 m / 75 s = 28 m/s

The Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of Amit's speed and Sumit's speed:

Factors of 50: 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50

Factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28

The greatest common factor is 2.

GCD(50, 28) = 2

Number of meeting points = (Amit's speed + Sumit's speed) / GCD(Amit's speed, Sumit's speed)

⇒ Number of meeting points = (50 + 28) / 2

⇒ Number of meeting points = 78 / 2

⇒ Number of meeting points = 39

**∴ The number of different meeting points on the circumference is 39.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__****Formula Used:**

Number of distinct meeting points (opposite directions) = Sum of ratio terms of speeds (in lowest terms)

**Calculations:**

Amit's speed = 2100 / 42 = 50 m/s

Sumit's speed = 2100 / 75 = 28 m/s

Now, let's find the ratio of their speeds and simplify it to its lowest terms:

Ratio of speeds = Amit's speed : Sumit's speed

⇒ Ratio of speeds = 50 : 28

So, the ratio of speeds in lowest terms is 25 : 14.

According to the formula: Number of distinct meeting points = Sum of ratio terms of speeds (in lowest terms)

⇒ Number of meeting points = 25 + 14

⇒ Number of meeting points = 39

∴ The number of different meeting points on the circumference is 39.
